```python
import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("VRPTW")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    n_customers = 9
    n_vehicles = 5
    Q = 50  # vehicle capacity
    vehicle_fixed_cost = 100.0
    depot = [50, 50]
    customers = [[49, 80], [32, 69], [14, 5], [61, 31], [35, 33], [46, 63], [21, 32], [23, 14], [50, 56]]
    demands = [16, 25, 6, 22, 14, 19, 13, 9, 6]
    time_windows = [[0, 323], [35, 93], [28, 102], [67, 153], [28, 93], [45, 141], [18, 73], [51, 108], [63, 151], [31, 112]]
    service_times = [13, 9, 11, 11, 7, 12, 6, 8, 9]

    # Node 0 = depot, nodes 1..N = customers
    N = n_customers
    nodes = list(range(N + 1))
    cust_nodes = list(range(1, N + 1))

    # Coordinates: index 0 = depot, 1..N = customers
    coords = [depot] + customers

    # COMPUTE distance matrix from coordinates
    dist = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                dist[(i,j)] = math.sqrt(
                    (coords[i][0]-coords[j][0])**2 +
                    (coords[i][1]-coords[j][1])**2)

    # Service time by node (depot = 0)
    svc = [0] + service_times

    # Big-M for time linking
    T_max = time_windows[0][1]
    max_svc = max(service_times)
    max_dist = max(dist.values())
    M = T_max + max_svc + max_dist + 1

    # --- Variables ---
    # Arc variables (binary)
    x = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Arc_{i}_{j}")

    # Load variables (MTZ subtour elimination)
    u = {}
    for i in cust_nodes:
        u[i] = m.addVar(lb=demands[i-1], ub=Q, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Load_{i}")

    # Time variables
    t = {}
    for i in nodes:
        a, b = time_windows[i]
        t[i] = m.addVar(lb=a, ub=b, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Time_{i}")
    # Fix depot departure to time 0
    t[0].ub = 0.0

    # --- Objective ---
    # Minimize travel distance + vehicle fixed costs
    obj = quicksum(dist[(i,j)] * x[(i,j)] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j)
    obj += quicksum(vehicle_fixed_cost * x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes)
    m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # --- Constraints ---
    # 1. Each customer has exactly one outgoing arc
    for i in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in nodes if j != i) == 1,
            name=f"VisitOut_C{i}")

    # 2. Each customer has exactly one incoming arc
    for j in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1,
            name=f"VisitIn_C{j}")

    # 3. At most K vehicles leave the depot
    m.addConstr(
        quicksum(x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes) <= n_vehicles,
        name="VehicleLimit")

    # 4. MTZ subtour elimination
    for i in cust_nodes:
        for j in cust_nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    u[i] - u[j] + Q * x[(i,j)] <= Q - demands[j-1],
                    name=f"MTZ_{i}_{j}")

    # 5. Time linking: if arc (i,j) is used, arrival at j >= departure from i
    for j in cust_nodes:
        for i in nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    t[i] - t[j] + M * x[(i,j)] <= M - svc[i] - dist[(i,j)],
                    name=f"TimeLink_{i}_{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

Subject: Daily delivery routing and scheduling challenge

Overview
We operate a fleet of identical delivery vehicles from a central depot to serve a set of customer locations within the same planning horizon. This memo outlines the operational challenge for building efficient same-day routes that meet customer commitments and return safely to the depot before the end of the day. All vehicles depart the depot at time 0 and, by policy, each vehicle runs a single outbound trip, visiting a sequence of customers before returning to the depot prior to the depot’s latest allowable time.

Travel time between any two locations is assumed to be equal to the straight-line distance between their coordinates, with unit speed so that distance and time use the same units.

Routing and scheduling challenge
Our task is to decide:
- Which customers each vehicle will serve, and in what visiting sequence.
- When each vehicle will arrive and start service at each customer, allowing for waiting if a truck is early.
- How to balance the number of vehicles deployed against route distances so that all customers are served once, on time, and within vehicle capacity limits, while ensuring every vehicle returns to the depot before it closes.

Operating rules and constraints
- Start and end of day:
  - All vehicles depart the depot at time 0.
  - Each vehicle completes a single tour and must return to the depot before the depot’s closing time; no mid-route depot visits or second runs.
- Customer time windows:
  - Each customer has an acceptable time window for starting delivery. Service must begin within that window.
  - If a vehicle arrives before the window opens, it must wait on site until the window opens.
- Service times:
  - Each customer requires an unloading/service duration. After service starts, the vehicle departs that location at arrival time + service time, or at window open + service time if it arrived early and waited.
- Capacity:
  - Vehicles have limited carrying capacity. The total demand assigned to any vehicle’s route must not exceed capacity at any point on the tour. Each customer is visited exactly once; split deliveries are not permitted.
- Travel times:
  - Travel time equals straight-line distance between locations at unit speed. Route timing must account for both driving and any waiting and service durations to ensure depot return before closing time.

Cost considerations
- Using a vehicle carries a fixed deployment cost in addition to costs proportional to distance traveled.
- Total cost for the day is the sum of:
  - The fixed deployment cost for each vehicle put into service.
  - The total travel distance across all active vehicles.
- The plan should avoid unnecessary vehicles and excessive mileage while preserving on-time performance and capacity feasibility.

Goals and success criteria
- Serve every customer exactly once.
- Start service at each customer within the specified time window and complete the required service.
- Keep the load on each vehicle within capacity limits at all times.
- Ensure every vehicle departs at time 0 and returns to the depot before the depot’s closing time.
- Minimize the combined cost of total travel distance and vehicle deployment.
